story.review_method: Read complete original and complete revision, compare changed paragraphs and preserved incident sequence. Prose review only; no illustration clearance.

observations: Independent reviewer opened all three current sheets at native resolution, originals and native detail crops; no material findings. Qualitative scale and grooming states remain provisional.

Neet four feet on waiting-room floor, gray Great Dane supported seated on floor with clear forelimbs/haunches, Buddy supported seated on bench. Closed carrier contains tabby, clear separate bodies and eye-lines. No sock still in Dane mouth, no procedure or premature gold tooth.
Final close body coats and restrained Neet nub/Buddy leg margins required; other animals provisional illustrative designs, not identity references for either lead.
Left Buddy torso-neck connectivity, four floor supports and seated Neet support visible. Finish should improve backward eyeline to Neet.
Right Buddy supported reclining on padded table with folded haunch, lifted forepaw and supported opposite paw. Labrador and terrier separate floor-supported bodies.
Sketch fur lines must not carry into torso finish.
Every current finished image opened at full resolution against original photos; concrete findings recorded per image.
Buddy has clear agency: he seeks reassurance, protects the Dane privacy, protects his blue toy, and accepts comfort from the vet. Neet remains exuberantly intrusive without erasing Buddy voice.
Gappy creates the wrong reassurance; private sock punctures the legend admiration; the blue-one claim interrupts abandonment panic with a crisp reversal. Paragraph spacing keeps those beats legible.
Waiting-room art follows the sock legend line and precedes the Dane denial; it reinforces admiring versus weary expressions without inventing an extracted sock.
Handoff image follows the explicit lowered-paw and sitting transition, with Buddy looking back before his reluctant step. No blue toy is invented; both dogs now match the stated narrative state.

Dream art follows Buddy paw-wave question and precedes the cool-dog/gold-tooth dialogue. It introduces neither gold tooth nor literal gravy boat; wavy border and ensemble differentiate dream from clinic reality.
Three images contribute ensemble misunderstanding, toy-ownership reaction and changed dream state; they are complementary rather than repeated anxious portraits.
The closing gravy-boat pickup concern carries Heather attachment through the absurdity and preserves Part 1 cliffhanger. The ending has clear space before editorial material.

Independent visual record accepts all three unchanged exact image hashes with no open anatomy findings. Reading-specific state discrepancy S031-RR-001 is now explicitly closed after rendered correction inspection.
Footer preserves manuscript Chapter 32, archive identity and explicit unapproved status; no alternatives omitted.
